cases.title: Panel: New lesson on a skill with a review due opens a lesson, not the review, and never mentions one

rubric.reason: The snapshot opened a lesson and the mentor opened it as one: it named the group ("Dot 2's Position, Opacity and Blurriness all run from 0.5 s to 1.5 s") and ended on the group choice, with no mention of a review, warm-up or anything being due; the four-weeks-ago line is plain memory, not a reason for a review.

The group is named in one sentence with real names and the shared time ("Dot 2's Position, Opacity and Blurriness all run from 0.5 s to 1.5 s"), the other kind is offered in one sentence ("Dot 1, Dot 2 and Dot 3 also all start at 0.5 s, if you'd rather stagger layers"), and the turn ends by asking the learner to choose.

Every name and time (Dot 1, Dot 2, Dot 3, Seal, Position, Opacity, Blurriness, 0.5 s, 1.5 s) appears in the offset_snapshot result, and "about four weeks ago" follows from days_since_practiced: 28 and the record's last_attempted.
